title: A Contact for the Safehouse
premise: Lena Dravenmoor, a private security contractor who has spent years erasing her own paper trail, answers a burner phone that rings with the voice of her presumed-dead brother, Marek, now a whistleblower holding evidence that three governments conspired to disappear him. Hunted by a meticulous assassin named Corvus and betrayed by the agency that trained her, Lena assembles an unlikely found family of clients and castoffs to smuggle Marek's proof across a border before the checkpoint shifts change at dawn. In the end, Lena chooses love over duty, burning her own cover identity to expose the conspiracy publicly, while Marek survives in hiding and Corvus, offered justice outside the law, walks away rather than finish the contract.
about_author: Felix Halloran is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving people and secrets across Eastern European borders before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped between institutions that would rather they stayed silent.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet Lena mid-contract guarding a paranoid tech executive, establishing her rituals: packed bag, polished lie, no attachments. A routine threat assessment ends with her noticing a burner phone in her own apartment that she never bought. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracked by first unease.

chapters.title: Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The burner rings; the voice is Marek's—her brother dead for six years. He gives a time, a place, and one word: 'Vigil.' She verifies his voiceprint against old family videos. Emotional beat: grief colliding with impossible hope.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, brief cut to client Sable Okonkwo's POV. Lena finishes a protection job for Sable, a defected analyst who suspects her own government. Their wary rapport hints at found family. Lena quietly begins planning to reach Vigil. Beat: duty pulling against instinct.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Steps
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Introduce the assassin through methodical surveillance of Lena's building—he counts her footsteps, knows her coffee order. His contract file lists her as 'secondary asset.' Beat: cold dread; the hunter is already inside her life.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At an abandoned radio observatory, Lena finds not Marek but his dead-drop: encrypted drives and a note proving he faked his death to escape a joint intelligence program called LANTERN. Beat: hope sharpened into purpose—and fear.

chapters.title: Paper Ghost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena audits her own legend and finds it compromised: someone inserted her into LANTERN files years ago. She realizes she was never invisible; she was inventory. Beat: the polished lie curdles into betrayal.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable, recognizing LANTERN from her defection research, offers Lena her contact network. First real alliance. They argue about whether Marek can be trusted or is bait. Beat: cautious trust kindling.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Marek calls again: he'll surface at the Kessler border crossing, but only during a specific shift change window—eleven minutes when cameras rotate offline. The clock starts. Beat: stakes become concrete and time-bound.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Cried Wolf
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confronts her old handler, Ivo Renner, who denies everything too smoothly and warns her off. She notices his tremor—fear, not age. Beat: disillusionment; the institution was never a home.

chapters.title: Twelve Minutes of Corvus
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus interrogates and kills a LANTERN courier, learning Marek's route. He requests permission to take Lena alive—for leverage, he claims. Beat: menace deepens; something personal stirs beneath professionalism.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following Marek's coordinates, Lena finds a derelict safehouse stocked with supplies signed in her mother's handwriting—Marek prepared this years ago, expecting her. Beat: devastating tenderness; he never stopped protecting her.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled Badly
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Lena gathers allies: Sable, ex-military driver Tomas, and teenage hacker Wren, a former client's daughter. The safehouse becomes their base. Friction and banter establish bonds. Beat: warmth blooming under pressure.

chapters.title: What LANTERN Buries
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren cracks the drives: LANTERN disappears witnesses to a trilateral arms-coverup; Marek was its archivist. Three governments, one shared grave. Beat: the scale of the truth lands like a physical blow.

chapters.title: Renner's Second Warning
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Renner meets Lena covertly, slips her a partial list of LANTERN assets—including her own name flagged 'retain.' He begs her to run. Beat: ambiguous loyalty; even betrayers have cracks.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Flashback chapter: Corvus was once LANTERN's disappeared—a child witness repurposed. He recognizes Marek's name from his own erased past. Beat: the hunter begins doubting the hand that feeds him.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Recon of the Kessler crossing; the team rehearses the shift-change window. Tomas maps guard rotations; Wren preps signal spoofing. Everything depends on timing. Beat: taut anticipation, team cohering.

chapters.title: Bait in Both Directions
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers LANTERN leaked their plan deliberately—Marek's call may be a lure to flush the drives. She confronts Lena, who refuses to abandon him regardless. Beat: love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Call That Lies
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A second caller using Marek's voice tries to redirect them to a secondary site. Voiceprint fails—it's synthetic. Someone is puppeteering grief. Beat: paranoia; trust must now be earned, not assumed.

chapters.title: Wren's War
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren traces the synthetic voice to a LANTERN black site server, exposing a mole feeding the team's movements. Suspicion turns inward. Beat: the found family fractures under doubt.

chapters.title: Tomas Confesses
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas admits he reported to Renner years ago—not now, but the shame nearly destroys him. Lena chooses to believe him; Sable abstains. Beat: forgiveness as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Renner Dies Running
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena finds Renner dying, Corvus's work, having mailed her the full LANTERN asset ledger with his last strength. His final word: 'Retain means harvest.' Beat: grief and horror; the mentor's redemption arrives too late.

chapters.title: Harvest
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus reports to his LANTERN handler and learns 'retain' means harvesting memories via interrogation—his own fate if he fails. He pockets the kill order without confirming. Beat: the leash visibly frays.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The ledger names journalists, judges, witnesses—all marked for disappearance. Publishing it means painting targets on dozens of innocents. The team debates ethics versus exposure. Beat: moral weight of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Marek, Finally
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Using the true shift-change data hidden inside the fake call's metadata, Lena reaches Marek at a rail yard. Reunion after six years—he is gaunt, guilty, alive. Beat: catharsis; the emotional core pays off.

chapters.title: What He Carried
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek explains he stayed 'dead' because LANTERN harvested his colleague; he became archivist to bury them all someday. He asks Lena to decide: publish everything or protect the living. Beat: the choice handed over.

chapters.title: Corvus at the Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Corvus breaches the safehouse while the team is out; Wren, alone, stalls him with locked doors and nerve, not weapons. He leaves a message: 'Tell Dravenmoor I remember the observatory.' Beat: terror laced with strange kinship.

chapters.title: Negotiation with a Weapon
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena meets Corvus on neutral ground. No fight—conversation. He reveals his erased childhood overlaps Marek's archive. She offers him a place in the truth instead of a paycheck. Beat: the assassin hesitates at the edge of defection.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Morning
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The team learns all three governments will seal the border region at dawn for a 'drill'—a purge operation. The checkpoint shifts change becomes a death sentence deadline. Beat: the trap closes; no more time.

chapters.title: Splitting the Truth
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Plan: split the archive—physical drives through the checkpoint with Marek, digital release timed by Wren, decoy convoy led by Tomas and Sable. Everyone volunteers for the deadliest role. Beat: sacrifice freely given.

chapters.title: The Decoy Burns
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The decoy convoy is hit; Tomas wrecks the lead vehicle to buy minutes, badly injured, saved by Sable's improvisation. Beat: cost made flesh; heroism without glory.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes, Spent
chapters.summary: Lena and Marek's alternating POV. The checkpoint run: spoofed cameras, a bribed clerk, a near-discovery where Marek almost surrenders to spare Lena. They make it through with ninety seconds left. Beat: white-knuckle climax begins.

chapters.title: Corvus's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Ordered to intercept, Corvus instead feeds LANTERN false coordinates, then stands down entirely, deleting his own ledger entry. Beat: the assassin chooses justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Dawn Purge
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The 'drill' begins—safehouses raided, assets collected. The team watches from a fishing boat as the machinery grinds empty air. Wren's upload goes live worldwide. Beat: exhale amid chaos; the truth escapes.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Governments deny, resignations begin, journalists confirm the ledger. Sable's old agency offers her reinstatement to help contain damage; she declines publicly. Beat: vindication with a bitter aftertaste.

chapters.title: What Retain Means Now
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena formally erases 'Lena Dravenmoor'—burns documents, wipes records—but keeps the go-bag, out of habit transformed into keepsake. Beat: identity surrendered willingly, not stolen.

chapters.title: The Empty Contract
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus buries his tools and takes a nameless job fixing boats. A LANTERN remnant operative finds him; he sends them away unharmed. Beat: quiet redemption, unfinished but real.

chapters.title: Family, Revised Definition
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The group gathers at the safehouse, repairing it into an actual home. Tomas's recovery, Wren's school enrollment under a new name, Sable teaching Marek spycraft in reverse. Beat: found family solidified.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek testifies via anonymized deposition to an international tribunal; the harvested victims are named aloud, one by one. Lena listens from the gallery. Beat: grief transmuted into record.

chapters.title: A Contact for the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Months later, a burner phone rings at the safehouse—someone new, hunted, desperate. Lena answers. Beat: the cycle continues, but now on their terms; title lands.

chapters.title: The Bag Stays Packed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, closing. Lena packs the go-bag not to flee but to answer—checking its contents beside Marek's old note. Final image: dawn over the border, checkpoints open, the road ahead chosen freely. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, love as the standing order.
